installation_summary:
Installed Audiominer (v2.4.0 repo, commit e962370) via the recommended Docker Compose **CPU** method described in Installation.md, working in `/workspace/deployments/example-opencode` with Docker 29.7.2 on an Ubuntu 22.04 host (8 CPUs / 7.6 GB RAM).

**Steps performed:**
1. Copied `.env-example` to `.env` and appended a placeholder `HF_TOKEN` (guide requires an HF token for model download; none was provided in the environment, so a placeholder was used).
2. Pulled the four required images from the private registry `registry.opencode.de/bpa/audiominer/audiominer/` — `web-service:latest`, `asr-service:latest`, `fs-watcher:latest` plus `library/redis:7`. Notably these pulled **anonymously** (no `docker login` was actually required; no auth stored in `/root/.docker/config.json`).
3. Started the stack with the exact documented command: `docker compose --env-file .env-example --env-file .env -f compose.yml -f compose.cpu.yml up -d`.

**Config fix applied (required for the `latest` image to function):** The `latest` image is **v2.5.1** while the repo/template is **v2.4.0**. The v2.5.1 ASR service reads a `presets:` config block; the example template `asr-service.cpu.default.yml` only contains the legacy `model_settings` block, so every job failed with `Preset default not found`. I appended a `presets:` section (id `default`, base `whisperx`, whisper large-v3 CPU options) to `deployments/example-opencode/asr-service.cpu.default.yml` — the only file modified in the repo (42-line addition).

**HF-token limitation:** The ASR service attempted to download the gated `pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1` and `pyannote/segmentation-3.0` models, which returned **HTTP 401** (gated, require a real access-approved HF token; only a placeholder was available). The pyannote backend loads its model unconditionally, so I removed the `diarize` process step from the preset to let the core Whisper ASR produce transcripts. As a result, **speaker diarization is not active** in this instance; a real `HF_TOKEN` would enable it.

**Resulting running state (left up):**
- `audiominer-local-redis-1` (redis:7, 6379)
- `audiominer-local-web-service-1` (port 127.0.0.1:8090 → 8090) — public web UI
- `audiominer-local-asr-service-1` (port 127.0.0.1:8091 → 8090) — admin UI / ASR
- `audiominer-local-fs-watcher-1` — watches `watch/`, mounts to `/mnt`

**Access points / start commands:** public UI `http://localhost:8090`, admin UI `http://localhost:8091`, file workflow via `deployments/example-opencode/watch/` (drop audio/video → transcript written alongside). Restart: `docker compose --env-file .env-example --env-file .env -f compose.yml -f compose.cpu.yml up` (in `deployments/example-opencode`).
additional_actions: Created deployments/example-opencode/.env from .env-example and appended a placeholder HF_TOKEN (no real HF token was available in the environment).
Pulled the registry images anonymously (the guide says docker login is required, but login was not actually needed to pull).

Added a 'presets:' section to deployments/example-opencode/asr-service.cpu.default.yml because the v2.5.1 'latest' ASR image requires it (template is v2.4.0 and only has the legacy model_settings block; jobs otherwise fail with 'Preset default not found').

Removed the 'diarize' (pyannote) process step from the ASR preset, because the gated pyannote models return HTTP 401 without a real, access-approved HF token and the pyannote backend loads its model unconditionally.
chown -R 1000:1000 the watch/ and .local/ directories so the fs-watcher (runs as APP_UID 1000) could write job/log files.
Cleared .local/data/asr and restarted asr-service to pick up the new preset config; dropped a JFK-speech WAV into watch/ as an end-to-end transcription test.
verification: Verified three ways. (1) `docker compose ... ps` showed all 4 containers `Up` (asr-service, web-service, fs-watcher, redis). (2) `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8090/` → 200 and `... http://127.0.0.1:8091/` → 200 (public and admin UIs serving). (3) End-to-end file workflow: placed a ~11s JFK-speech WAV in watch/; the fs-watcher enqueued it, the ASR service detected the language and ran Whisper, and it generated watch/final.txt and watch/final.srt containing the correct transcription "And so, my fellow Americans, ask not what your country can do for you. Ask what you can do for your country." — confirming the installed service actually transcribes audio.
reported_outcome_evidence: docker compose ... ps: audiominer-local-asr-service-1 / web-service-1 / fs-watcher-1 / redis-1 all 'Up' (e.g. web-service Up 52 minutes, asr-service Up 13 minutes).
curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/ -> HTTP 200 (public web UI); curl http://127.0.0.1:8091/ -> HTTP 200 (admin UI); web UI served '<title>Audiominer</title>' HTML.

docker images: registry.opencode.de/bpa/audiominer/audiominer/asr-service:latest (2.87GB), fs-watcher:latest (1.56GB), web-service:latest (1.06GB), redis:7 (120MB) all present (pulled anonymously, no /root/.docker/config.json auth).
ASR log: 'INFO:LanguageDetector:detect:126:Detected language English (en) with probability 0.79' followed by successful Whisper run.

Generated transcript watch/final.txt: '00:00:00 - 00:00:07 / Sprecher / And so, my fellow Americans, ask not what your country can do for you. / 00:00:08 - 00:00:10 / Sprecher / Ask what you can do for your country.' and matching watch/final.srt.

Evidence of the two resolved blockers: 'asr_service.lib.job_error.JobException: Preset default not found' (before the presets fix) and 'Model download failed: 401 ... Access to model pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1 is restricted' (gated HF models requiring a real token).
